🔖 Ethereum price charges toward $2,000 as Nasdaq rally revives demand 

🔔 Ethereum price has climbed from $1,800 to an intraday high near $1,945 after a technology-led Wall Street rebound revived risk appetite, although resistance below $2,000 has kept traders cautious.

⚠️ According to data from cryptonews, Ethereum price traded near $1,929 at the time of writing, about 6% above its July 21 low. Buyers initially followed U.S. equities higher as the Nasdaq Composite gained 1.3% and the S&P 500 added 0.9%, led by semiconductor and artificial intelligence stocks. Micron rose 12.2%, while Nvidia advanced 2%. Notably, enthusiasm around upcoming technology earnings drove the session.

👀 Momentum also improved against Bitcoin. Crypto trader Daan Crypto Trades noted that ETH has outperformed BTC during the third quarter after falling 29.26% in the first quarter and another 25.28% in the second. CoinGlass data shared by the trader showed Ethereum up 22.98% so far in Q3, compared with an average third-quarter return of 8.86% since 2016. According to Daan, the rebound followed Ethereum’s weakest first half since 2022, making the recovery less unusual despite Q3’s historically slow performance. 

🔗 Bitcoin’s ability to retain its recent gains therefore remains relevant to ETH’s next move. A fresh Bitcoin sell-off could drain demand from altcoins even if Ethereum continues to outperform on a relative basis.

🔊 Iranology Foundation chief meets Saudi, Pakistani envoys to expand academic cooperation

📌 Tehran, IRNA – The head of Iran’s Iranology Foundation held separate meetings with the ambassadors of Saudi Arabia and Pakistan on Sunday to discuss expanding scientific and cultural cooperation, while also exchanging views on regional developments and the importance of diplomacy.

Ali Akbar Salehi, president of the Iranology Foundation, met Saudi Ambassador Abdullah bin Saud Al-Anzi in Tehran, where he said cultural diplomacy could foster mutual understanding, build trust and promote sustainable cooperation among regional countries.
​
The two sides also discussed developments in West Asia and their implications for regional cooperation. They stressed the importance of political dialogue, regional cooperation, mutual respect and diplomatic mechanisms to reduce tensions and preserve regional stability and security without foreign interference.
​
Salehi and the Saudi envoy also agreed to maintain consultations and make greater use of cultural and academic capacities to strengthen bilateral relations.
​
In a separate meeting, Salehi received Pakistan’s newly appointed ambassador to Iran, Imran Ahmed Siddiqui. The two sides highlighted the longstanding historical and cultural ties between the two countries and called for broader cooperation between academic and research institutions.
​
The discussions covered cooperation in Iranology, historical studies, academic exchanges, joint scientific conferences and efforts to promote the two nations’ shared cultural heritage. They also exchanged views on regional developments, emphasizing dialogue, diplomacy and regional cooperation as key to maintaining peace, stability and security and easing regional tensions.
